fanny.accroche: A blade dancer on the battlefield.
lore: A blade dancer on the battlefield. Fanny is the younger sister of Tigreal, who grew up under the protection of her family and older brother since childhood. But Tigreal took responsibility for a mistake in combat and left home. Despite her family's obstacles, Fanny joined the army, and with her own designed weapons, she successfully completed one task after another, becoming an exceptional fighter capable of taking care of herself. === Lore === Fanny Wertz is the youngest daughter of the Wertz family and the youngest sister of Tigreal. Although the men of the Wertz family served in the military for generations and guarded the Moniyan Empire, the women of the family were never allowed to join the military. From the point of view of the men in the family, their duty was to protect the country and the family from threats, and the women were to stay away from war.

So, since she was a child, Fanny had been invited to study painting and design. The elders in the family hoped that she could become a famous artist or designer and help run the family business. But Fanny considered this unworthy of her. For as long as she can remember, Tigreal was Fanny's greatest hero. She also hoped that one day, like her brother, she could fight on the front lines for the Imperial Army and guard the empire.

Growing up, Fanny, active and rebellious, became a nightmare for her guardian. She was very fed up with these out-of-date lessons. She often ran away for various reasons and had a weakness for dancing with weapons: but Fanny was so intelligent that even if she was tired from her lessons, she managed to understand in a very short time. Tigreal showed extreme affection to her rebellious sister. Every time Tigreal returned to Lumina City for repairs and maintenance with the army, it was Fanny's happiest day, because Tigreal not only told her peculiar anecdotes and exciting stories from battlefields of various places, but also taught her useful combat skills, which made Fanny even more eager for military life.
However, Tigreal firmly refused Fanny's desire to join the army as he always did. He didn't want his only sister to be in danger.

Out of love for his younger sister, Tigreal promised that when Fanny turned 18, he would take her to the Order of Light base to show her what it's like. This expedition therefore had a special meaning for Tigreal and Fanny. However, as Fanny waited day and night for her brother's triumphant return, news arrived from the front lines: although the battle against the border demons had been won, Tigreal, who led the Second Division of the Order of Light, had left its ranks for unknown reasons and disappeared.

As the empire held a national holiday, the Wertz family entered into a crisis. For a time, deserters and cowards replaced heroes and commanders, and these words became synonymous with Tigreal. The Wertz family, once famous throughout Moniyan, has been discredited. On the one hand, she adored her beloved brother, and on the other, damning rumors were flying. Faced with all this, Fanny fell into confusion, but after the confusion, she said to herself in her heart: my brother is not a coward, much less a deserter. In his absence, I must stand up and reinvigorate the glory of the Wertz family.

Subsequently, despite fierce opposition from her mother and other elders, Fanny resolutely chose to join the army. She wanted to use her actions to protect the dignity of her brother and the Wertz family. But it didn't go as well as she had imagined. When Fanny arrived at the barracks, she was greeted with laughter and mockery: the soldiers were full of prejudices against this pampered noble lady, and life in the barracks was much more difficult than she imagined. The heavy training and the lack of material conditions make the task difficult for Fanny, accustomed to a privileged life. For this reason, Fanny got rid of her long hair that she loved, devoted twice as much effort to training, and passed the recruitment test. She was incorporated into the reconnaissance unit of the imperial garrison.

Several years after the start of her scouting career, Fanny had truly grown and transformed. As an Imperial scout, Fanny often needed to travel between various steep mountains or other difficult terrain. In order to overcome her physical and strength flaws, she inconceivably learned from Tigreal, combining her combat skills with the design knowledge she had previously acquired by designing and constructing for herself a pair of long swords with steel cables. When she pulled the trigger, the steel cables shot out from the handle, latched onto the target, and pulled Fanny towards her. After endless practice, Fanny finally mastered the sword, and with it, she shuttled between the cliffs, gracefully traversing all kinds of difficult and complicated terrain, successfully completing her missions again and again. His performance not only convinced those who were full of contempt and prejudice towards him before, but it also earned him respect and prestige. For her graceful and exquisite figure as she danced in the air, the soldiers kindly called her the “Blade Dancer.”

Thanks to her exceptional performance in the garrison, Fanny finally obtained the necessary qualifications to be selected into the Order of Light. Even more surprising, Tigreal, his older brother who had been away from the Moniyan Empire for many years, also returned to his homeland from the distant Northern Valley. Seeing what her sister had done for the family, Tigreal praised Fanny, believing that she had become a great warrior, and invited her to stay by her side and fight side by side.
Travelers in the Land of Dawn, if you see a person flying in the mountains and forests like a free bird, you have surely seen the graceful and swift figure of Fanny.
anecdotes: Fanny's name could be derived from the word "Fanny" (short for Frances or Stefanie), but it could also come from the Germanic word fannen, meaning "to capture" or "to seize", which corresponds to her fast and aggressive style of play.

His surname "Wertz" is a popular Germanic surname, either derived from the Old English personal name Hwit, meaning "the white one", or derived from the Middle High German word "wert" meaning "river island" or "river bank".
Fanny's appearance and fighting style resemble soldiers from the Attack on Titan (進撃の巨人) series. Coincidentally, she also has a collaborative skin, Mikasa, with the series.
Fanny is the most difficult hero according to Hero Difficulty Level, being the only hero with a difficulty level of 10 out of 10, the highest of all heroes.
The next hero Hirara will join the list soon.
She is the first hero to use energy as a source of skills.
She is the only hero without any form of crowd control on her kit, not even a slow effect.
Her "Skylark" skin is inspired by a type of lark bird known for its high-speed flight and agility, perfectly matching Fanny's fast, aerial fighting style.
Claude and Fanny are among the few heroes in Mobile Legends to have multiple couple skins, with Fanny's "Lifeguard" and "Heart Afloat" being among her romantic-themed skins.
She shares her Japanese voice actor, Ono Saki, with Hanabi.

faramis.accroche: A Necrokeep necromancer determined to find a cure for the Mist.
lore: A Necrokeep necromancer determined to find a cure for the Mist. A gifted doctor who came to Necrokeep to study the mysterious plague. Instead of finding the key to controlling life and death, he met Vexana, the Duchess of the Cursed Earth and the girl who had twice brought sunshine to his dark life. Vowing to find a way to reverse the curse and repay Vexana's kindness, Faramis willingly eroded himself by the Mist and used himself as a specimen for his research. === The Fearless Soul === Faramis comes from a long line of doctors. Using the ancestral staff passed down through the family, his grandfather combined magic and medicine and developed cures for many formerly incurable illnesses. This feat earned the talented physician a title from the Moniyan Empire, and the family had since served the royalty as their personal physicians.

However, none of these proved enough to earn the family's respect from his equals. The other nobles viewed them as simple servants with special medical skills, while young Faramis, for this reason, was often bullied and ridiculed by his peers.

At a banquet the boys knocked again and poor Faramis was left passed out on the garden floor. When he regained consciousness, he saw a high-born girl half-kneeling beside him, giving him medicine. It was the only time young Faramis received kindness from his peers. The meeting, although brief, was like a ray of sunshine in his gloomy life.

Frail and sick since birth, Faramis came close to death on numerous occasions and only survived thanks to the meticulous treatment of his parents. After numerous near-death experiences, he vowed to conquer death and take life into his own hands and was reluctant to serve the royalties as his family did.

He found the little evils of royalties extremely annoying and wanted nothing to do with these hypocritical nobles. He aspired to tackle complex and incurable diseases to take his skills to heights that no other doctor had ever reached before.

With this goal in mind, Faramis left Lumina City and embarked on his journey alone, solving inexplicable illnesses one after another along the way, not under the care of a doctor, but to explore the possibility of going beyond life and death.
Upon learning of the Necrokeep incident, Faramis believed he had found the perfect integration of life and death and immediately headed to the city, searching for the key to controlling both.

Protected by his ancestral staff, Faramis found himself immune to the Mist that was ravaging the city. He passed through a crowd of desolate inhabitants and came upon Duchess Vexana, ruler of the ruined fortress. She prepared and distributed "Moonlight Brew", a moonlight herb remedy that was said to be the "cure" for the erosion of the Mist.
At first, Faramis thought it was all a big lie: she was just playing an ignorant and hypocritical role like the other nobles.
Until that moment, Vexana had put the last "Moonlight Brew" into her hands without hesitation-Faramis was stunned. This was tantamount to abandoning his “hope of living”.
The “hypocrite” really wanted to save everyone.
Looking at the noble lady in a new light, Faramis couldn't help but think of his brief encounter with the kind girl in his childhood...

The Mist was nothing like the incurable illnesses Faramis had encountered before. After many failed attempts, he finally achieved breakthrough by infusing magic into herbs. And with every progress he made, he insisted on testing the effects on himself. Except his fragile body could only handle so much abuse. He soon began to experience the consequences of his experiments, eventually passing out in his laboratory.
Lying on the cold ground, Faramis felt his life draining away quickly. He clenched his fists and tried to get up, only to find that he couldn't even open his eyes, his consciousness gradually fading.

Faramis never thought he would be able to open his eyes again, and when he did, he saw a young woman bending down, parting her lips to let a bitter liquid fall into her mouth. Confused, Faramis discovered that this image overlapped with his memory of the girl in the garden. Looking at the strange but familiar face, Faramis recognized that she was the same noble girl who had helped him back then.

The girl who had brightened his childhood had once again come to his aid! During his recovery, Faramis found himself falling in love with the young woman who had saved him from the darkness twice. She was the only person who never abandoned him, except for his parents.

However, as soon as Faramis recovered, Vexana urged him to leave the area, saying that it was dangerous for a living person to continue to stay in Necrokeep. The Mist was beginning to master his enchanted staff. If he stayed much longer, he would soon meet a fate like theirs.

Faramis doesn't say a word; his eyes were fixed on the moonlit grass and the withered staff in his hands. His reason told him that it was time to leave, but when he stood in front of the castle door and saw the forced smile on Vexana's face, he found himself unable to leave like that. Memories of the childhood encounter and the meticulous care given to Necrokeep flashed through Faramis' mind. He could not abandon the young woman who had twice brought light and warmth into his life. He had made his choice, he would stay in Necrokeep and complete the task at hand.

Faramis abandoned the protection of his staff, finally plunging into the scourge of the Mist. His skin turned yellowish and pale, and yet he felt no fear. He knew he could defeat this scourge. And to do this, in order to discover the secrets of life and death, he must experience the curse himself.
This time it was her turn to get Vexana out of the misery she found herself in.
=== Wedding in the mist ===

Faramis finally received a skin ("Royal Magus") on October 24, 2022, which is the longest time for a hero to receive a second skin, in a period of 3 years, 5 months and 6 days or 1,255 days. floryn.accroche: A kind-hearted girl determined to spread greenery across the world.
lore: Belerick discovered the decline of Agelta's barren lands during one of his many meanderings long ago.

Despair and sorrow almost consumed him, when a small blooming flower suddenly appeared before his eyes. “There is still life!” Driven by such tenacious vitality, the treant decided to create on the spot what was later known as the Oasis.

When creating the Oasis, Belerick unintentionally poured more power into the little flower, and the overflowing energy condensed into a light seed. The little flower, however, has undergone an even more peculiar transition. He transformed into a life form that had never appeared in the Land of Dawn – Floryn.

Since the day she was born, Floryn had never left the Oasis. The latter isolated her from the harsh environment of the desert, allowing her to live a carefree life. For Floryn, this luminous seed was the only mystery of her peaceful life. She spent the days contemplating the secret of the seed and the nights sleeping in the shade of the leaves. Only explorers and caravans occasionally visited this quiet little world.

Among the caravans that frequented the Oasis, Floryn met a young man with a bright smile. He told Floryn amusing stories he had seen or heard during his trip each time he came to stay at the Oasis. As their friendship deepened, so did Floryn's trust in the young man. She showed the young man the luminous seed, hoping that it could help her solve the riddle.

At first, the young man wholeheartedly helped Floryn search for information about the seed. However, over time, Floryn discovered that the young man always avoided her gaze and changed the subject whenever the seed was brought up. Floryn began to worry about the young man's condition.
One night, Floryn woke up with a start. She was shocked to find that the seed she had always carried with her was gone!
Floryn searched everywhere in the Oasis but to no avail. Torn with anxiety, Floryn went to the young man for help, only to discover that he had already left the Oasis with his camel.
A thought that Floryn dreaded to believe came to mind: could it be him?
Floryn followed the young man's footsteps out of the Oasis. She wanted to find out the truth.

However, what awaited her was a silent response to what she had seen and heard along the way. It was Floryn's first time entering the desert, and also the first time she saw the howling sandstorms and the look of despair on the people's faces. Before that, she never understood what kind of suffering people outside the Oasis experienced.
When Floryn caught up with the young man from her village, what appeared were cracked farmlands, dried up wells, starving children...and these desperate children who would stop at nothing to survive.

The young man was slumped in a corner. He had wanted to sell the seeds to feed his family, but he never expected that the seeds would wither as soon as they left Floryn. As a result, those who were willing to bid would not pay a single penny.
The young man returned the withered seed to Floryn, ready to take responsibility for betraying their friendship.
Floryn, however, doesn't say a word.

The experience along the way had given Floryn insight into the difficult situation the young man found himself in. Compared to the sadness of being betrayed by her friend, another, even stronger and more complicated emotion was bubbling in her heart. Driven by this emotion, Floryn really wanted to do something for the earth, to save people who lived in extreme poverty like the young man.

A wave of magical power surged from the depths of Floryn's heart. It flowed down her arm and into the seed she held in her hand. feeling the power, the once faded seed shone again, and from the light a hundred times more dazzling than before emerged a cute and living little creature!

This little creature jumped into the air and eagerly displayed its miraculous powers; he summoned rain with a flick of his tail, and new shoots gradually grew from where the rain fell. The once lifeless village was surrounded by greenery in just a few minutes.

Floryn was stunned by the sight before her. She had never imagined that the seed could give birth to such a magical creature, just as she had never thought that it would one day leave the Oasis. It was only when Floryn's determination to change the wasteland resonated with Belerick's will within the seed that the latter awakened its true power.
Even though the little creature born from the seed was still very young, Floryn saw, with its limited power, endless possibilities to change the desert.
"You look like a round drop of dew. I should just call you Dew!"
Dew surrounded Floryn enthusiastically, as if she appreciated her name too.

The changes in the environment brought light back to the villager's eyes. The young man also promised Floryn that he would never stray from the right path again. Bidding the young man farewell, Floryn and Dew moved on to their next stop.

Today, thanks to the tireless efforts of Floryn and Dew, the Oasis is growing at considerable speed. And this greenery will eventually spread throughout the desert, dispersing all desolation and despair.
anecdotes: Floryn was the 8th and is one of the heroes offered free to players upon release. Other heroes offered for free are: Faramis, Belerick, Silvanna, Luo Yi, Benedetta, Mathilda, Phoveus and Edith.
It is quite possible that Floryn is based on Flora, the Roman goddess of flowers and spring.
Floryn's design and skills reflect a nurturing and supportive role, which further ties her to themes typically related to a character inspired by flora or nature spirits.
Floryn is the first hero to heal his allies anywhere on the map.
She is the only one to upgrade another hero by placing another item on him.
Like Belerick, she can also create life; in her case, she created Dew.

Floryn's "Yatai Waitress" skin is inspired by the Japanese word "Yatai" (屋台), which refers to street food stalls in Japan that sell ramen, takoyaki, and other delicious treats. These stalls are often manned by friendly vendors wearing traditional Japanese aprons and kimonos, just like Floryn in this skin.

Floryn has similarities to Filipino “Diwata” (fairies/guardian spirits) and Southeast Asian folk creatures. Diwatas are mythical nature spirits or deities in Philippine folklore, often compared to fairies, nymphs, or guardian deities of other cultures. They are known for protecting nature, bestowing blessings, and sometimes punishing those who harm the environment.
She shares her Japanese language voice actor, Gōto Ayasa, with Kagura, another hero with a Poke specialty and a high level of control effects.

franco.accroche: Brave permafrost warrior, Bane's sworn enemy.
lore: The harsh natural environment of the remote, wintry North Valley has shaped those who live there into a brave and martial people. They revered the strong and were proud of their tall and sturdy appearance. They believed that their sturdy physiques were inherited from their common ancestor, the Golem of Iceland, who once ruled these lands.

But for the young Franco, this traditional way of thinking was only oppressive. His tribe had lived on the coast of the Frozen Sea for generations and relied on its large fleet of trading and fishing ships to support themselves. But the passing years have not made young Franco want to become an adult man. They only pointed out the strange way the others looked at him. Although his father was a famous harpooner throughout the coast and his brothers were all tall and strong, Franco was small and unimpressive for a Nord. Some even joked that, given Franco's stature, his ancestor was not the Icelandic Golem, but the dwarves of legend.

To train powerful warriors, the Northern Valley tribes located on the coast of the Frozen Sea engaged in intense competitive play from childhood and received systematic combat training once they reached puberty, so that they would be ready to engage in lengthy trading missions or fishing voyages as adults. However, much to Franco's embarrassment, while the other boys had already begun to wield battle axes, spears, and rig sails, he could only wield much smaller weapons. In fact, the battle axes were even taller than him.

Although small in size, Franco had a great ambition: to become the greatest warrior in the Northern Valley, and see his name engraved in the book of heroes, to be adored by future generations. To achieve this ambition, Franco trained tirelessly, day after day, increasing his strength and martial prowess. Yet despite Franco's intense training, he was looked down upon by others due to his small size. Even his father and brothers thought that little Franco was only meant to be a merchant, and never a warrior or sailor capable of facing a cruel environment and fierce enemies.

Faced with constant mockery and discrimination, Franco angrily decided to leave his tribe. He would prove to everyone that, even though he was small, he could still achieve big things. Over the next few years, he hid in the endless mountains of the North Valley, surviving and training alone in this most extreme environment. After long years of fighting against the bitter cold, terrible beasts and omnipresent threats, Franco has developed strength far beyond that of an ordinary man, as well as a firm and indomitable character.

While Franco trained alone in the mountains, the cruel and power-hungry Captain Bane descended on the frozen sea. Breaking the long-respected rules of the pirates and fishermen of the North Valley, he began to invade and annex the territory of other pirates as well as commoners, ruling them with an iron fist. Those facing Bane's mighty fleet and fearsome firepower had only two options: submit or be annihilated.

Bane's cruelty was met with fierce resistance from various forces, the fiercest of all coming from Franco's tribe. As a warning to those who would challenge him, Bane sent a massive armada of pirate ships to blockade the surrounding sea and launched constant raids on Franco's tribe, declaring that he would sink all their ships and raze their harbor.

After ten years in the mountains, Franco returns to his tribe, full of confidence and strength. Engaging in a fierce battle, he crushed Bane's men with his anchor and his divine strength. It was only after the battle that the members of his oppressed tribe made a surprising discovery: that the hero who had come to save them was none other than the once-mocked little Franco. After learning of Bane's treacherous actions, Franco angrily vowed to annihilate him and all of his henchmen.

Franco then led his tribesmen and their ships in resistance against Bane's cruel rule. They outfitted old fishing boats with battering rams and cannons, and attacked Bane's pirate fleets wherever they found them, dealing a heavy blow to Bane's forces. In desperation, Bane assembled a huge fleet to quell Franco's resistance, but the two sides remained in a stalemate after several battles, with Bane unable to gain the advantage. Once, Bane managed to lure Franco into a trap, but only succeeded in injuring him, and Franco managed to escape with his life. Furthermore, more and more residents of the Northern Valley, inspired by Franco's courage and strength, united around him to fight Bane.

Seeing Franco's strength growing by the day, the cunning Captain Bane hatched a plan: he would sue for peace with Franco, suggesting that they search for the Twilight Orb of legend together, while secretly luring the Moniyan Empire's navy to the frozen sea. This would allow him to kill two birds with one stone: find the Twilight Orb and defeat Franco for good. Wary of Bane's sudden goodwill, Franco pretended to take the bait, ordering his men to search for the Orb of Twilight, while secretly leading a contingent of warriors to take control of a pirate ship among the Black Shark fleet.

Bane instigated a battle between the two marines, preparing to reap the benefits afterwards. However, Franco, hiding within the Black Sharks, ordered his men to open fire behind Bane, hitting the Behemoth directly. In his most exultant moment, Bane and his flagship received a fatal blow from the defiant lord and sank to the bottom of the sea.

Once Bane was drowned, Franco became ruler of the entire Northern Valley coast. He led his people in driving out the remnants of Bane's forces, rebuilding the port, and reviving trade, bringing a renaissance to the entire Northern Valley.

Out of respect for Franco's glorious achievements, the people of the Northern Valley nicknamed him the Frozen Warrior. But for Franco, everything he had done so far was still not worthy of such praise. Shortly after, Franco learned that Bane not only had not perished, but had gained new power and was gathering his men to make his return.
anecdotes: Franco is based on a real-life historical Viking warrior.
Franco and Lesley have the same quote: “One hit, one kill.”
Miya had the same quote but was removed due to her redesign for the NEXT project.

Most of his quotes are taken directly from the character York from Magic Rush: Heroes, with whom he also shares the same voice acting. This explains why some of them seem completely foreign to him, like: "I love the smell of gunpowder in the morning."
Franco is currently the only hero whose voice lines come from Magic Rush, while previous heroes with the same case have been replaced.

Franco was temporarily banned from the game on December 29, 2021 after an exploit was discovered in the Serpent's Lair. The ban was lifted on January 19, 2022 for a duration of 21 days and 3 hours, which is the longest recorded ban in MLBB history, prior to Helcurt's ban in 2023.
Franco is one of three heroes capable of applying crowd control Suppression, the other being name=Kaja and name=Barats.

fredrinn.accroche: A master treasure appraiser in Los Pecados is accumulating wealth and searching for his lost friend.
lore: “Be darling and pour me a glass of your signature drink,” the drunken bum insulted the bartender. “And I’ll tell you the truth about that bastard Fredrinn!”
The people of Los Pecados had long memorized stories about Fredrinn, but his name was still like a siren's call, drawing all who heard it to its source.
“Two shots for our good friend,” said a young smuggler, throwing a handful of pennies on the counter.
"Ahh, very good gentleman. I'll make it worth your while while I assure you. This one is something you'll never have heard of!" Exclaimed the tramp.
Everyone in the bar had their eyes on the filthy tramp, except for the man who was drinking alone in the hidden corner, a compass clutched tightly in his hand.

“The story begins over a dozen years ago,” the tramp began, looking surprisingly sober after taking a sip of his drink. "After receiving his fiefdom, Duke Vance of Castle Grandrock opened the sea trade route to Northern Vale. Merchant ships coming from the north... all laden with rare goods... and all trading exclusively with the Duke. Well, the old weasel was practically bathing in profits!"
The tramp took another sip, looking around at the greasy faces waiting impatiently for more.

“But wealth and prestige brought little pleasure to the Duke,” he continued. "If anything, this new wealth only awakened in him an even greater desire: to climb to the top of the imperial nobility. The Duke began to discipline his children with strict rules, punishing any child who dared to disobey his words."
"For once, I'm damn glad I'm not the son of a rich moron!" the smuggler intervened.

“Yes, and you wouldn’t be alone,” replied the tramp. "One of Vance's boys gave the Duke a never-ending headache. This youngster had no interest in the rules and etiquettes of nobles, and had a desire for freedom and adventure. The Duke didn't want this kid's bad ideas to infect the minds of the other children. So, he arranged for the boy to study at the Monastery of Light."
“Quite a practical excuse to make fun of the monastery’s archbishop!” the bartender intervened.

“Well, you would be right,” replied the tramp. "As the Duke was in dire need of stronger political allies. The boy, however... had other plans. Having heard his father's arrangements, the little rascal decided to sneak out of the castle and embark on his own adventure."
“I don’t think the Duke would have much to fear, though,” the smuggler interjected again. “A spoiled little brat like him, he would soon go back to his daddy!”
“Yes, the duke understood that,” replied the tramp. “Old Vance was really mad, but he didn’t even bother to look for his boy!

"The kid, however, turned out to be much tougher than his father expected. He was not an adventurer, mind you; but through his courage, wit, and excellent judgment, the boy managed to overcome every obstacle that came his way. He had a particular penchant for exploring the most dangerous areas yet unexplored by man.
"And soon, his name spread throughout the Land of Dawn. Yet no one knew about his past life."
The tramp paused for a long time, as if waiting for a response. But all he got were blank faces and glassy eyes.
“Oh, you’ve got to be kidding me…” he grumbled with a sigh and a roll of his eyes. "The boy was Fredrinn... Fredrinn Vance!"
His revelation was met with a new round of silence. But when his audience caught on, the tavern erupted into an uproar.
"Fredrinn...a nobleman!? Why, that punk is a damn crook!" A burly man with a horned helmet, his eyes bulging, they almost popped out of their sockets.

“No one knows this money scammer better than me!” the man exclaimed. "No matter what you prepare in advance, the leech will always demand a higher price. Well, a gang leader himself barged into his store to personally deliver his payment, a loaded gun pointed right between Fredrinn's eyebrows. The bastard didn't even flinch...and instead demanded more money!"
The young smuggler raised his hand. "But is it true what they say about him? 'A no-questions, no-disclosure policy' about his valuation of hunted treasures?"

“Yes,” the burly man replied. "No matter who you are, this scoundrel sticks to his guns. It is not possible to compel him, not even by force. What are you going to do, attack his treasure shop? Then prepare to be beaten - according to the customs of Los Pecados. And if you are lucky enough to wake up, all damaged items must be paid for in double, not a single penny less - "
“Come on, we all know about this!” cried the tramp, his voice dripping with sarcasm. "But what about Fredrinn's secret!? That crystal lodged in his chest—"

The crowd fell eerily silent, only to erupt into wild cheers moments later. Even the bartender poured the tramp another shot to get him to talk. "The crystal is said to come from the ruins of a lost civilization. It seals an ancient power coveted even by the King of the Abyss. Fredrinn went to great lengths to get his hands on this crystal, even killing his own partner in the process..."
The man sitting in the corner approached, interrupting the wanderer's words.

His muscular figure towered over everyone in the tavern. His eyes burned with disdain as he looked at the lesser men around him. Embedded in his scarred chest, right where his heart was, a strange crystal pulsed with a ghostly glow.
"F-F-Fredrinn..." the tramp and the burly man stuttered in awe.
The tin wine box in Fredrinn's hand creaked as his fist clenched.
"A wonderful story, my friend," Fredrinn said calmly. “However, if I hear someone say that I killed my partner again… I will come to their door and give them a thorough assessment.”
Fredrinn walked out of the bar after those words, his blood and his memory coursing through him.

The astute and revered treasure appraiser of Los Pecados was once a passionate and adventurous boy who wanted to escape his noble status. There was always a friend at his side who was ready to do anything with him… Fray.
Except Fray was gone.
During their last adventure together, the two came across an ancient altar. A giant crystal hovered at its center, radiating an ominous glow.

Fray warned his partner, but the young and reckless Fredrinn could not escape the lure. He approached the altar and placed his hand on the crystal, thus disturbing the balance of an ancient protection.
A ghostly figure dressed in a black cloak emerged from the center of the altar.
“…You two will be the final offering”
These were the last words Fray and Fredrinn heard before the altar began to collapse under the weight of ancient magic, trapping them in the middle of the chaos.
“Fredrinn…this time it’s my turn to save you…”

Fray, who had always been hiding behind Fredrinn, picked up a shard of crystal and pressed it against Fredrinn's chest, giving him the only chance of survival. The crystal's power integrated with Fredrinn's and protected him from collapse. But when he looked up, he found Fray and the ruins gone without a trace. The only thing left was Fray's magic compass.
Fredrinn found a new quest the moment he opened the compass. The blue pointer recorded Fray's life trace. It spun wildly and vibrated like tiny heartbeats.
Fray is still alive!

To search for clues that could help locate Fray, Fredrinn remained in Los Pecados as a treasure appraiser. He has accumulated his funds to build a vast intelligence network gathering all knowledge related to the ruins.
The cost didn't matter.
Standing in front of a wall of clues, Fredrinn looked at the magic compass in his hand.
"As long as the pointer is ticking, I will not give up."
anecdotes: "Fredrinn" sounds like Frederick, a Germanic name meaning "peaceful ruler" (frid = peace, ric = ruler).
The release of a new hero, Joy, took 98 days to succeed Fredrinn, making it the longest interval between hero releases.

He was originally supposed to have a baseball bat instead of a sword. Early drafts suggested that Fredrinn would wield two short swords instead of a single large blade. The developers opted for a heavy sword to emphasize its raw strength and precision.
He loves adventures and currently resides in Los Pecados.
First tank with a “combo-based” mechanic. Unlike most tanks, Fredrinn relies on the chaining of several skills to activate his ultimate, Appraiser's Wrath.
His design and personality resemble rogue adventurers or mercenaries, similar to characters like Indiana Jones, Flynn Rider (Tangled), or Gambit (X-Men).
One of the few MLBB heroes with a delayed ultimate activation. His ultimate requires skill combos first, which differentiates him from tanks who can instantly use their ultimates.
Some early concept sketches made him look more like a pirate captain than a noble adventurer.

lore: What is the Valkyrie?
“What is the Valkyrie?” As smoke began to rise from the hallowed halls of Sessrumnir, this question – which had haunted Freya's thoughts for so long – surfaced once more in her troubled heart.

"...The Valkyrie is a legacy." When Freya was just a child, her sister Skuld, newly chosen to become the next Valkyrie, took her small hand in his, and together they grasped the ancient sword and shield. Little Freya could not yet understand the fierce light that burned in her sister's eyes, but she felt, for the first time, the deep weight of the sword and shield pressed against her palms.

Fate, however, is a cruel and fickle thing. Years later, Skuld perished during a perilous mission, and with his death came the disappearance of the Heart of Aurora, that sacred relic preserved in Sessrumnir for countless centuries, the very embodiment of the strength and heritage of Northern Vale. The people mourned Skuld's sacrifice, but whispers began to creep through the blizzards like poison: some dared to call Skuld a failure, an incompetent Valkyrie who had betrayed the North Valley itself. Freya spoke no words in her sister's defense. Instead, she simply tightened her grip on her sword and shield, as if shaking her sister's hand again.

She stepped out into the howling, endless blizzard, her heart determined to recover the lost Aurora Heart. She would never allow her sister's hands - hands worn from protecting others - to be stained with the mark of betrayal, nor would she allow the sacred title of "Valkyrie" to disappear into the vast and merciless blizzard.
Sword in hand, Freya marched across the endless expanses of Northern Vale, gathering the myriad answers to a single, haunting question: "What is the Valkyrie?"
Ordinary people whispered that the Valkyrie was salvation incarnate. She had raised her blade amid the bloody feuds of the Garland tribe, saving Hilda and her parents from certain doom.

Battle-scarred warriors proclaimed the Valkyrie to be glory manifested. Hadn't she braved the dangerous Frozen Sea, forging an alliance with Franco to protect innocent fishermen from Bane's incessant attacks?
Yet countless others in the North Valley have declared that the Valkyrie is faith itself, for within the hallowed halls of Sessrumnir burns a forge powered by the sacred Heart of Aurora.

Here, for the first time, Freya discovered the true genesis of the Valkyries' legacy: eons ago, when the world was young, the Frost Giants erected a mighty forge deep in the snowy wilderness to challenge the two gods themselves, blessing the North Valley with eternal spring. But the wrath of the gods was swift and merciless: the glaciers descended like divine judgment, shattering the forge and leaving the northern lands shattered and bloodied. It was only when Sigrun, the first Valkyrie - a half-giant of legendary prowess - wielded a fragment of the Twilight Orb called the Aurora Heart to reignite the dying embers of the forge, that Northern Vale caught its breath. Sigrun entrusted this sacred power to the bravest of warriors, charging them with guarding both the homeland and the Aurora Heart. Future generations would know them by one revered name: Valkyries.
Through the howling wind and swirling snow, Freya stared at Sessrumnir in the distance. It remained cold and silent, like the heart of Northern Vale, frozen and still.
Although her relentless pursuit had yet to reveal the whereabouts of the Aurora Heart, Freya was getting closer and closer to the terrible truth behind her sister's sacrifice.

The glaciers, born of the divine will of the God of Light, had attracted countless followers who transformed them into fortresses, extending the dominion of their divinity across the realm, even inadvertently fostering the birth of the divine maiden Aurora. After the end of the Endless War, these followers of light disappeared like ghosts, only to resurface years later with nefarious intent. They set cunning traps that cost Skuld his life, and in the chaos that followed, the Aurora Heart disappeared into legend. Yet the dark ambitions of the cultists remained undiminished: they sought to drain the very essence of the forge and destroy it completely, eliminating all obstacles to the inevitable return of the God of Light.
Thick, choking smoke was escaping from the sacred halls of Sessrumnir!

When Freya reached the battlefield, Sessrumnir was in total ruin. The followers of the light greedily siphoned the power of the forge with reckless abandon. The warriors of the North Valley fought desperately against overwhelming odds, while the aurora-colored flames in the forge flickered weaker and weaker. Deep tremors shook the very foundations of the country: everything teetered on the brink of collapse...

Spotting Freya's arrival as reinforcement, the followers of light prepared to flee like cowards. Every fiber of Freya screamed to pursue them, to seek revenge on her fallen sister, but the power of the forge was draining, requiring its presence to safeguard the very survival of Northern Vale.
How to choose between revenge and duty? Freya's gaze fell on those dying flames of dawn—
Blacksmithing required food; only a new energy could reignite his sacred fire.
— With determination burning in her heart and defiance coursing through her veins, Freya rushed toward the dying light of the forge.
"...What is the Valkyrie?"
In the swirling dance of dawn and flame, the ethereal form of her sister Skuld materialized once more, her spectral hand tenderly clutching Freya's.
“You have already given your answer.”
Freya finally understood the radiant light that had always burned in her sister's eyes.

For a thousand years, when the two gods cast their glacial curse to freeze the North Valley in an eternal winter, the people kept the forge burning and built the mighty walls of Sessrumnir around it. Generation after generation of Valkyries had fought in these hallowed halls, bled and died here. They faced death without fear, knowing that the roaring flames of the forge would transform their essence into weapons of unimaginable power, to pass on to the next Valkyrie.
Now Freya too has accepted this eternal duty and thrown herself into the flames.

Her sacrifice earned her the recognition of the collective will of all the Valkyries who had come before her, whose spirits still resided in the forge, but in truth, she had long since earned the blessing of Northern Vale. Not through the Aurora Heart, but as Sigrun, the very first Valkyrie: with the aurora as her guide and the tundra as her witness, Freya carved her glory from wind and ice and transformed her body into an invincible weapon.

Freya's sword and shield, held tightly in her grip, were reforged like a halberd amidst the roaring flames, while golden wings spread majestically behind her. After passing the final test, she returned to Sessrumnir as the glorious Valkyrie. With her sword raised high, she pursued the fleeing followers of light: it was her revenge, her duty and her answer.
“I am a daughter of Northern Vale and I will defend this land to the death!”
anecdotes: Freya is based on the goddess Freyja, a goddess from Norse mythology. It is associated with love, beauty, fertility, sex, war, death and magic.
Freya's appearance in lore is based on a Valkyrie. Valkyries are female figures who guide the souls of the dead to the Valhalla hall of the god Odin.

First generation Freya is a paid hero. Additionally, Freya is one of two heroes (including Odette) who cannot be purchased with Battle Points. However, Odette was purchased by Battle Points back in the day when it was released in 2017. Until now, Freya was only purchasable with diamonds. The reason for this is still unknown.
English voice actor Freya also voiced some of Battlefield's rapid-fire chatter.

pouvoirs: Bringing the fallen warriors to Valhalla

lore: Gatotkaca the "Mighty Legend" was the son of Bima and Arimbi of the Arcapada universe. Since his childhood, he has been a champion of the Gods and fights the evil enemies of his homeland.

Gatotkaca once lost in battle and was beaten near death, but he rose again as a mighty warrior of the Pandava clan and gained supernatural power after training within Candradimuka, the Cauldron of Heaven. With his Antakusuma armor and Braiamusti-Braiadenta gauntlets, he can fly through the skies like lightning and hunt down his sworn enemies, the wrathful Asuras.
Gatotkaca, the Knight of Pringgadani, is a symbol of bravery and devotion. Based on the comic series “Garudayana” created by Is Yuniarto and inspired by traditional Indonesian shadow puppets.
anecdotes: Gatotkaca is based on Bharatyuddha, a Javanese adaptation of the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata. According to the creator of the Garudayanas, Is Yuniarto, its design is inspired by wayang, a traditional Javanese shadow theater. Wayang is used to retell epics including Bharatayuddha.

His most recent skin, "Tide Preserver", was released on January 8, 2024, making him the hero who received the skin for the longest period, 1745 days, between it and "Spark", released on March 30, 2019.
His vocal lines "Om Telolet Om" are a social media meme that depicts the excitement of young Indonesians when a bus driver honks rhythmically as they pass by.
Gatotkaca shares his Japanese voice actor, Abe Daiki, with his rival Martis, and with Helcurt, who shares his recommendation on the roaming route.

gloo.accroche: A magical amalgamation of cute and mischievous creatures that dwell deep within the Shadow Swamp.
lore: During a massive war in the Barren Lands, the Second Regiment of the Moniyan Empire was almost completely wiped out. Among the sea of ​​corpses scattered all around, a Moniyan soldier had managed to survive; but he lost all his comrades and had to return alone to his native country.
Dark clouds shroud the Barren Lands year after year. Without the sun, moon, and stars to guide his path, this lone survivor became lost and lost in the Shadow Swamp.

The land and water found in the forests of Shadow Marsh are corrupted by the Abyss, leaving the place damp and putrid. The man's extreme hunger and fatigue, along with the endless forest around him, plunged him into darkness and despair.
As he was about to pass out, a strangest sensation made him regain consciousness: a sticky sensation spread down his back, then he lost all control of his limbs which ran wildly on their own.

He would describe this moment in his memoir as feeling like he was just a wooden puppet, like those played by the Moniyan children. He was manipulated by an invisible force, rushing nimbly through the forest at incredible speed.
The man was about to lose consciousness when the body he no longer controlled stopped. Coming to his senses, he looked with wide eyes at what was before him...

There he saw the ruins of a great temple surrounded by vines, weathered by wind and frost but still grand and imposing. These ancient temple ruins stood out like a sore thumb in the surroundings of Shadow Swamp.
The strange feeling running down his spine faded when he stopped, but that's when he saw something small jumping into the nearby bushes, seemingly hidden.

Could this thing be behind all this? The soldier was determined to get to the bottom of this and moved in the direction the figure was taking. A loud rustling sound emanated from the vegetation, and it seemed as if some sort of violent struggle was taking place inside.

And as the soldier advanced furtively, reaching out to push aside a branch, there appeared before him a small creature the size of a charcoal briquette; he prepared to catch it and study it more closely, but before he could act, countless others had appeared from everywhere. They piled up neatly, and in just over ten seconds, the creature no bigger than a lump of coal had transformed into a mighty beast. This struck fear into the heart of poor soldier Moniyan who fainted on the spot. But when he awoke once again, he found himself no longer in the swamp, but on the border of the Drylands and the Empire.

Back in the empire, he regaled everyone with this tale. The citizens of Moniyan had great respect for this veteran, but considered his story to be mere hallucinations of a man consumed by fatigue after having narrowly escaped death.

After all, even the most erudite scholars of Moniyan had never heard of such a creature. There was little the soldier could do except write his experiences down on paper, as the evidence that would be discovered later might prove his sanity.
As luck would have it, he didn't have to wait that long. This dream came true while he was still alive and healthy.

When the Elvish text "Azrya" reached the Magic Academy, a student of the Moniyan Empire read records within a faction called Gloo - records directly consistent with the experiences of that Moniyan soldier he had read about before.
The curious student sought out the dean of Ulturia School, Eudora, who, after reading through the soldier's writings, confirmed that they did indeed describe an encounter with Gloo.

After hearing it from Eudora, humanity became aware of the existence of the Gloo, special beings with special ways of life. Thanks to a mysterious secretion, once just one of them had attached itself to a living being, they could then begin to completely envelop it.

Additionally, their gel-like outer covering acted as a conscious organ that allowed unique neural networks to function between individual “Goos,” forming the larger “Gloo” sensation. Among these beings, some would occupy higher roles within the network, commanding all others when they combined into a single form. By merging into different numbers[,], they were able to control their size and shape at will.

The Goos were shown to be intelligent and pure beings, proud of their shared "group wisdom" which was mainly used to play pranks on neighboring Elves. When she heard about Private Moniyan's bizarre adventure, she realized what had happened: a group of Goos must have wandered too far away, and so they clung to him as a larger organism to hitchhike home.

Since his birth, the Goos had never ventured outside of Azrya, instead guarding the forests and the mysterious old temple. They had never initiated any sort of battle, at most taking the form of a terrifying beast to frighten away any outsiders who accidentally entered their territory. Even the Elves who lived nearby knew little about their species.
Perhaps Goo's greatest intelligence could be seen in the fact that they resided in the depths of the forests, living in peaceful harmony with the rest of the world.
However, the Abyss changed everything.

Taking refuge in the ancient temple, Goos strove to maintain his rationality and faith, to avoid becoming like the nearby Dark Elves who had fallen into his clutches. But a deep, dark corruption spread within them and their forest as the Abyss wielded its power.
Eudora was by no means unaware of Goo's predicament. At the end of Soldier Moniyan's writings, she left a few sentences.

"The Abyss is a catastrophe. It divides factions and breeds pure hatred. But maybe, just maybe, it is a chance for us: a chance for all the souls of these lands to come together once more, to become one."
When the destinies of all people are linked, where will sweet Gloo go next?
anecdotes: The name Gloo is a pun on the word "Glue", referring to his Grab, Grab for sticking to an enemy hero.
Gloo is the second hero who can attach to another hero and use her skills while attaching, the first being Angela.
Gloo is the first hero to attach to an enemy hero, while Angela attaches to an ally hero.
Gloo was originally called Daktec.
Gloo's favorite fruit is the apple.
Gloo is the second hero to have a base skin with skill effects, the other here is Guinevere.

gord.accroche: Dean of the Icarus School of the Magic Academy.
lore: Gord has always been the living proof of excellence within the magic academy. He was born with the gift of manipulating mystical powers, which allowed him to master several sophisticated spells at a young age. But it's clearly a double-edged sword as Gord has become more and more arrogant over time. One day, he came across a banned book at the academy that recorded the method of forging pure mystical existence from the human body using mystical powers.

The young wizard buried himself in the book and threw himself into his study without respecting outside opinions. It worked successfully at first, pure mystical energy began to flow through Gord's veins, allowing him to cast even more powerful spells. Unfortunately, Gord was unable to control this power and was overwhelmed by the mystical energy. Gord then tried to seek a solution from ancient magical sources. With the combination of the two different energies, Gord's body was almost devastated. With the help of Elward, the chief wizard, the turbulence in his body could finally be controlled. The incident had a huge impact on Gord, leaving his body half red and half blue. Although he was saved, Gord would never again be able to control the magic contained in pure mystical energy.

Elward encouraged Gord until he finally got back on his feet. Elward then invited Gord to continue his career as a wizard and invited him to teach at the academy. After careful consideration, Gord accepted the offer. He wanted to find a student who would continue his studies without making the same mistakes. From that day on, Gord began a new life as the strictest teacher in the magic academy.

granger.accroche: A mysterious demon hunter who operates outside the conventions of the Church of Light. Always seen with a violin case in hand, he hunts down demons with his two soul-devouring weapons.
lore: A bard, a famous demon hunter Granger, a demon hunter who is somewhere between human and demon, always preferred to stay alone. But if anyone could enter his world, they would realize how terrifying it is: the incessant screams and shrill screams constantly deafen his ears and his heart. When he draws his demon-eating weapons and unleashes a hail of bullets, the demons' agonizing screams become a requiem playing deep within his soul. Only the intertwining of their death cries and the sound of gunshots can drown out the noise that torments him every day. Every shot Granger fires is not only her performance against the Abyss, but also an expression of her lament. === Bullet Sonata === An unnamed city on the border of the Moniyan Empire is Granger's destination for this trip
He walked leisurely, the bright red scarf around his neck exuding a strange aura. His skin was as pale as parchment, with a high collar covering half of his face, revealing only a pair of dark eyes.

Granger headed towards the outskirts of the city, fully aware of what awaited him. Even though their deep growls were hard to hear, the ringing in his ears that he despised was growing louder and louder.
Suddenly, a familiar melody caught Granger's attention. A child sits in the street and plays a tune on a flute. It is the “Hymn to the Light”, a song he often heard when he was young.
Granger's childhood was tragic, to say the least.

One night, his city was attacked by demons. With nowhere to escape, Granger's parents hid him in a small space under the floorboards. As the demons burst in and dragged his parents away, their screams and demonic growls left an indelible shadow on his young heart. This memory turned into a constant ringing in her ears, torturing Granger night after night. The pain caused him to withdraw from others and he became more and more reclusive. Until the day when a beautiful and sweet melody calmed the ringing, like a warm hand on his heart, granting him a moment of peace that he had almost forgotten.
For the first time, he stepped out of his chaotic world and looked up to see a priest playing the violin.
“What is the name of this room?”
The priest took a pen and paper from his pocket and wrote the words "Hymn to the Light."

It turned out that the priest was once the choir leader of the Monastery of Light. It was his job to soothe people's suffering hearts with his voice. But years ago, when Alice infiltrated Lumina City and threw the city into chaos, the priest was struck by a demon and lost the ability to speak. But instead of falling into despair, he picked up the violin and continued to help others through music.
Perhaps the sound of the violin was too inviting. Granger left his world and followed the priest to the monastery. He even tried to learn the violin but could only produce discordant noises.

"It seems like I have no talent," Granger lamented dejectedly. The priest smiled and showed him that true melody does not come from talent, but from kindness and perseverance in the heart, and in this aspect he thought Granger had a lot of it.

Granger, who failed to make much progress in music, showed exceptional talent in hunting demons. The leaders of the Church personally invited him to join the ranks of their demon hunters, even offering him a specialized weapon: a pair of demon-eating pistols capable of absorbing demonic energy and converting it into special bullets for killing demons. The few friends he had, including Alucard, invited him to hunt demons together, but Granger refused. Even though the priest's music had healed his chaotic world, the night of his parents' deaths still remained in his heart like a permanent wound, bleeding at the slightest touch.

The priest respected Granger's decision. He believed that even the deepest wounds could heal one day and that this introverted and gentle child would eventually accept the past and move towards a better future.
But that day would never come.

Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss, led his Abyssal legions through the Moonlight Forest to attack the Moniyan Empire. In response, the Church of Light recruited demon hunters to prepare for the impending war. Seeing Granger disturbed by this, the priest let him take leave of the monastery to decide his future. Whether or not he chooses to remain a demon hunter, the monastery will always be his home.
But when Granger returned to the monastery, he saw only burning ruins and the priest lying in a pool of blood – the demons had already struck.
Whatever he chose, it no longer made sense.

The priest's hand still held the violin bow. Granger could almost imagine the priest calmly performing his final requiem as the demons attacked. The ringing invades his world again. But this time, there would be no Hymn to the Light to appease him. There would be no one to smile and comfort his pain, no one to play him a lullaby to help him sleep. How could he silence this piercing noise... this creeping madness... this deafening rage in his chest?

Sensing the presence of a living soul, the demons stationed nearby moved closer. Granger took out her weapons and began a frenzied 'performance'. As the screams of the demons grew louder, the sound of the bullets also grew louder. The two cacophonies intertwined in a grand requiem, drowning out the ringing in Granger's ears. He suddenly realized that for him, it was the only way to ease the pain. Blood for blood, until all evil is dead and gone.

After that, Granger officially became a demon hunter. He named one of his pistols "Dirge", modified the other into a cannon and installed it in the priest's violin case, which he named "Requiem". He wrapped bandages around his hands to prevent bloodshed from staining the hands that once hoped to learn the violin. From then on, every hunt became a requiem for those he lost.
The memories that had resurfaced were shattered again.
Granger's attention returned to the present. Since he set foot in this small town, the ringing in his ears hasn't stopped, but he knew that everything would calm down soon.
He crouched down and gently placed a few coins in front of the child.
As the “Ave Maria” reached its finale, the Demon Hunter’s Death Sonata was about to begin.
anecdotes: While "Granger" originally meant "farm steward", it also sounds like "Ranger", which fits his lone wolf and marksman personality. His name could be inspired by The Gunslinger (Stephen King's Dark Tower series), which features a similar gun-wielding anti-hero.

He has French and Italian roots.
His weapon name is Dirge and his barrel name is Requiem.
His Ultimate (Death Sonata) is named after a piece of classical music, corresponding to his experience as a violinist.
Its design is heavily inspired by Western gunslingers, mixed with anime and gothic elements.
He carries a violin case and calls it a guitar case but it's loaded with cannons. One of his deleted vocal lines "Don't you dare touch my guitar case". But it's actually a violin case.
He speaks French in his voices.
He actually plays music with his gun on his violin case during the encore.

Granger's Doomsday Terminator skin is heavily inspired by The Terminator film series. Its cybernetic design, glowing red eye, and robotic enhancements resemble the T-800 (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger).
